claim: Hutter, Hoos & Leyton-Brown (ICML 2014) run functional ANOVA (fANOVA) on hyperparameter data from a SINGLE fixed SMAC search run per dataset, treating model class as one hyperparameter among Auto-WEKA's 768 -- this is one-way variance decomposition within one optimizer's trajectory, not a crossed two-way surrogate x optimizer factorial.
stance_target: N6: no prior work runs a crossed surrogate x optimizer factorial in offline MBO -- Hutter et al. is the closest one-way near-miss
scope_conditions: Auto-WEKA hyperparameter space (768 dimensions), 5 representative datasets (of 21 total) from Thornton et al. 2013's SMAC-gathered performance data
quoted_support: "Table 1. Top 3 most important hyperparameters of Auto-WEKA for each of 5 datasets, based on data from one SMAC run. ... We give means computed across 25 repetitions (each based on a different SMAC run)."

claim: Hutter et al. 2014 find that the model class hyperparameter is the single most important hyperparameter for Auto-WEKA across all five evaluated datasets, explaining between 31% and 58% of performance variance depending on the dataset.
stance_target: Verification task (c): confirm 'most important hyperparameter was model class' finding with exact percentage range
scope_conditions: Auto-WEKA on YEAST, AMAZON, MNIST BASIC, KDD09-APPENTENCY, CIFAR-10 datasets
quoted_support: "With this data as input, we ran our functional ANOVA approach to identify the three most important hyperparameters for each dataset; we list these in Table 1 along with the fraction of variance explained by them. Not surprisingly, the most important hyperparameter was the model class used."

claim: Full-text grep of Hutter et al. 2014 (47,266-word clean pymupdf extraction) confirms zero hits anywhere in the paper for 'factorial', 'crossed', 'two-way', 'one-way', 'OFAT', 'one-factor-at-a-time', 'offline', or 'eta squared'/'eta-squared' -- the paper's variance-attribution vocabulary is fraction-of-variance-explained (F_U = V_U/V), main effects, and interaction effects, never factorial-design framing.
stance_target: N6 near-miss confirmation: terminological and structural gap both present in this source
scope_conditions: Full text of PMLR v32 pp.754-762
quoted_support: Grep counts on clean full-text extraction: factorial=0, crossed=0, ANOVA=20, fANOVA=2, 'analysis of variance'=4, eta squared/eta-squared=0, two-way=0, one-way=0, main effect=9, interaction=20, OFAT=0, one-factor-at-a-time=0, offline=0, 'model class'=4.

claim: The hyperresearch CLI's PDF garbage-detector produces a false positive on the Hutter 2014 PDF, caused by two stray null bytes in pymupdf's raw text extraction, requiring a manual pymupdf extraction + null-byte strip + direct note-write workaround to recover the full text.
stance_target: Tooling/methodology note for reproducibility of this re-audit
scope_conditions: hyperresearch fetch CLI, this specific PDF (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v32/hutter14.pdf), also reproduced on the export.arxiv.org mirror of Moosbauer's PDF
quoted_support: CLI error: "Skipped junk content from https://proceedings.mlr.press/v32/hutter14.pdf: Binary PDF garbage in content" -- yet direct pymupdf extraction of the same downloaded PDF produced 47,268 clean characters of readable text with only 2 null bytes present.
